corta: the bank of faders runs off the left and right edges and off the bottom — no console body, no room, no operator is ever visible, only the channel strip itself
escena: SCENE (production suite at night, extreme macro): a long bank of identical channel faders fills the lower half of the frame, cropped hard left and right. EVERY fader is pulled all the way DOWN to zero — a dead flat line of forty identical caps, their scales unlit. ONE fader, just right of centre, is pushed ALL THE WAY UP: it stands alone above the flat line, its channel strip the only one with a glowing cool blue level showing. The eye lands on that one raised fader first, then reads the dead flat row it is standing in. A hard low raking light from the left skims across the caps and throws a row of sharp parallel shadows; the light dies before it reaches the upper half. A small orange sculpture sits at the far right end of the strip, cropped by the edge. 100mm macro lens at f/4, focus on the raised fader. CRITICAL FRAMING: the ENTIRE UPPER HALF of the frame — everything above 50% of the frame height — is one single dark, evenly toned surface with NOTHING in it: no object, no screen, no lamp, no window, no light beam, no bright spot, no shadow edge. All action, all light and every bright patch stay strictly BELOW the middle of the frame. The whole frame is COOL and contemporary: daylight-neutral white balance, blue-leaning shadows, nothing warm, amber, golden or tungsten anywhere, no retro glow — the ONLY warm colour in the entire picture is the small orange sculpture itself. Everything except the sculpture is completely unbranded and no text anywhere is readable: the channel markings are tiny, angled and shallow-focused.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near edge of the console apron running along the very bottom against the lens

texto.muro: the dark unlit upper section of the console housing, evenly toned and free of any light, its matte finish visible
